# MCP Runtime documentation
> Open-source Kubernetes control plane for deploying and governing MCP servers. The CLI generates Kubernetes resources; allow-list policy checks tool calls through the gateway and records decisions. Observe mode records calls without enforcing policy.

## Start here

- Quickstart: https://docs.mcpruntime.org/hosted-quickstart/ — Deploy a sample server on the hosted platform, grant an active managed agent access, and connect through the adapter.
- Getting Started: https://docs.mcpruntime.org/self-hosting/ — Install MCP Runtime on your own Kubernetes cluster.

- Learn overview: https://docs.mcpruntime.org/learn/ — Guided path from core concepts through a first server and multi-team setup.
- Module 1: https://docs.mcpruntime.org/learn/01-core-concepts/
- Module 2: https://docs.mcpruntime.org/learn/02-first-governed-server/
- Module 3: https://docs.mcpruntime.org/learn/03-multi-team-access/

## Use MCP Runtime

- Publish an MCP server: https://docs.mcpruntime.org/publish-mcp-server/ — Generate metadata, build and push an image, deploy, and verify the server.
- Agent adapters: https://docs.mcpruntime.org/connect-clients/ — Enroll a session-bound certificate, configure the local HTTP proxy, and pass OAuth tokens when the target uses OAuth.
- MCP authorization: https://docs.mcpruntime.org/mcp-oauth/ — Configure the optional authorization server and OAuth resource settings.
- Multi-team isolation: https://docs.mcpruntime.org/teams-and-access/ — Team namespaces, RBAC, NetworkPolicy, and cross-team grants.

- Cluster readiness: https://docs.mcpruntime.org/cluster-readiness/ — Check registry trust, DNS, TLS, storage, and ingress prerequisites.
- Cluster provisioning: https://docs.mcpruntime.org/cluster-provisioning/ — Provision the reference Kubernetes topology, with K3s as the worked distribution example.
- Public reference deployment: https://docs.mcpruntime.org/reference-deployment/ — Operate the complete Runtime and external identity-provider deployment: configuration, updates, backups, recovery, and verification.
- Runtime: https://docs.mcpruntime.org/runtime-operations/ — CRDs, reconciliation, image resolution, ingress, and rollouts.
- Platform services: https://docs.mcpruntime.org/platform-services/ — Gateway policy, audit events, analytics, and observability.
- Troubleshooting: https://docs.mcpruntime.org/troubleshooting/ — Diagnose deployment, access, registry, analytics, and cluster issues.

## Key concepts

- `MCPServer` describes a server and declares its tool metadata. The operator creates the workload and route; the gateway can evaluate policy before requests reach the server.
- `MCPAccessGrant` is standing policy for a server and human, agent, or team. It sets tool rules, allowed side effects, and a maximum trust level.
- `MCPAgentSession` is a Kubernetes resource for a time-bounded delegated identity, consented trust, expiry, and revocation. It is not an OAuth token.
- The gateway requires a matching grant under allow-list policy. A session is required when `session.required: true`; `server init` enables this by default. The default allow-list decision is `deny`.
- `policy.mode: observe` records decisions but does not enforce grant, session, trust, or side-effect checks.
- Managed agent IDs are generated by the platform agent directory. Use an active `agt_<26-character lowercase ULID>`; a display name is not an ID.
- The adapter presents its certificate during the HTTPS handshake. OAuth, when enabled for the target, is a separate bearer token on each HTTP request. For adapter calls, the token subject must match the session human.
- The adapter's default local listener is `127.0.0.1:8099` and does not authenticate local clients. Share it only with clients using the same Runtime agent identity.
- The gateway evaluates declared tool metadata; it does not inspect the server implementation. Tool names and side-effect declarations must match the actual server tools.
- Trust levels: `low`, `medium`, `high`. Side effects: `read`, `write`, `destructive`.
- Platform modes and publish scopes: `tenant`, `org`, `public`.
